D018-D001_h001.question:
It’s hard to put everything into words, but for at least the past year or so I feel like my mind doesn’t work the way it used to. I’m retired now and live alone, and I spend most days by myself on purpose. I don’t really pick up the phone when friends call anymore; I just don’t have the energy or interest to chat.

What bothers me most is how these memories keep popping into my head out of nowhere. I can be washing dishes or trying to read, and suddenly I’m right back in that moment, like it’s happening again. I can’t seem to push it away, and I keep thinking, “If only I’d done something different, maybe it wouldn’t have happened.” I go over that in my head a lot.

I feel on edge much of the time, like something bad is about to happen. The smallest noise can make me jump, and then my heart races and my hands shake for quite a while before I settle down. My thinking feels sort of foggy—I lose track of what I’m doing, can’t follow the thread of a conversation or a TV show, and it takes me a long time to get myself focused again.
D018-D001_h001.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D018-D001_h001.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D001_h002.question:

Certain sounds or situations just hit me harder than they should. For example, if someone walks up behind me in the office or comes quickly around a corner, I jump way more than seems normal, and my heart just races. Sometimes something small will remind me of what happened, and it’s like my brain locks onto it — I get really upset, almost like I’m back there emotionally, even if I know I’m not.

I’ve also stopped doing a lot of things I used to enjoy. I used to love weekend trips to photograph old buildings, but now I just don’t feel like going anywhere. I keep going over everything in my head, thinking I should’ve handled things differently, that it was partly my fault.

On top of that, my focus is terrible. I misplace my phone, my keys, the project files — I’ll open a drawing set and forget what detail I was supposed to fix. It’s like I’m there physically but my mind keeps slipping away, and I honestly can’t tell if it’s always been this bad or if I’m just noticing it more now.
D018-D001_h002.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D001_h002.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D001_h003.question:

I also notice I’m oddly unmoved by my own accomplishments. A successful opening, a good review—I shrug it off, tell myself anyone could’ve done it. A lot of the time I end up replaying everything and thinking, “If they hadn’t done what they did, none of this would have happened,” and then I spiral into this heavy, embarrassed feeling about the whole thing and about myself, like there’s something fundamentally shameful I can’t shake.

D018-D001_h020.question:
I work with the big cats mostly, and ever since that incident with the escaped leopard a while back, I just can’t seem to switch off. Even when I’m at home on the couch, I feel like I’m bracing for something to jump out at me. My wife says my shoulders are always tight, like I’m on duty 24/7.

Little things set me off. If I hear metal gates clanging or animals suddenly screeching, my chest tightens and my mind goes straight back to that day. Sometimes even walking past the enclosure where it happened makes my heart race, so I’ve been trading shifts or finding excuses to be in another part of the zoo. I also avoid talking with the coworkers who were on shift then; I’ll change the subject or go check on some “urgent” feeding.

I keep catching myself blaming the management for cutting corners on staffing and safety, and resenting the handler who was supposed to be watching that lock. At the same time, I’m struggling to keep my mind on tasks—feeding schedules, meds, paperwork. I lose track mid‑routine, misplace tools, and have to double back to check if I actually locked a gate or just thought about locking it.
D018-D001_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D001_h020.answer: B & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D001_h021.question:
I guess the main thing is, my body still freaks out before my brain catches up. I’ll be on set, and if someone slams a metal door or a car backfires, my chest just tightens, my heart’s pounding, palms sweating. Sometimes it’s just seeing a certain alley or that particular kind of handheld camera light—my stomach drops and I have to step away, pretend I’m checking a shot.

I’ve carried this heavy sense of being… tainted, I guess, for a long time. The stuff that happened on that shoot overseas—I keep thinking I should’ve done something different, that it says something awful about who I am. When one of my films does well, I still feel like a fraud. Crew congratulate me, and I just nod; there’s no real pride, just this numb “okay, what’s next.”

I also snap more than I used to. If someone on my team misses a cue or questions a decision, I go off—raised voice, swearing, really going at them. Afterwards I feel guilty, but in the moment it’s like a switch flips.

Focus is a mess too. I lose track in meetings, reread the same line in a script over and over, jump between email, rough cuts, texts. I don’t know if it’s always been like this or I’m just noticing it more lately. It’s been going on at least the last few years, getting harder to ignore.
D018-D001_h021.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D001_h021.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D001_h022.question:
I’ve been struggling for maybe… a couple of years now? It’s hard to pin down exactly when it started. I work as an insurance agent, so I’m on the phone a lot, reading through policies, answering emails, and my mind just slips away. I’ll catch myself rereading the same paragraph three or four times, or zoning out in the middle of a client call and then panicking because I’ve missed what they said. It’s not every day, but enough that my performance reviews have mentioned “focus issues.”

Sleep’s a problem. I get these dreams that feel way too real—same kind of situation over and over, and I wake up with my heart racing and this awful feeling like I’ve done something wrong. I don’t always remember all the details, just the fear and this deep sense of shame that kind of hangs over the next day.

I snap a lot more than I used to—like my daughter spills juice or someone cuts me off in traffic and I just explode, then feel stupid and guilty afterward. Even when something objectively good happens—a bonus at work, a nice weekend away—I feel weirdly flat, like I’m watching someone else enjoy it and I can’t quite access that feeling myself.
D018-D001_h022.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D001_h022.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D001_h023.question:
I work as a social media manager, so I’m online all the time, and it feels like my brain just doesn’t switch off anymore. For about… I don’t know, months now, maybe longer, I’ve been on edge all the time. The smallest thing sets me off—someone changing a brief last minute, a notification sound—I snap or feel like I’m going to.

Sometimes it’s like I’m not really in the room. I’ll be scheduling posts and suddenly I’m back in that situation from a few years ago, like it’s happening again. I can see it and feel it, and for a few seconds I forget where I actually am. It’s like I’m watching it through my own eyes again, not just remembering.

I can’t shake this constant feeling that what happened was somehow my fault. Even when people tell me it wasn’t, I keep replaying what I could’ve done differently. And even when good things happen—a campaign does really well, I get positive feedback—I just feel… flat. I know I “should” be happy, but it doesn’t land.

On top of that, focusing is really hard. My mind jumps around during meetings, I miss details in briefs, and I reread the same email three times before it sticks. I’m not even sure when that started; it just feels like my attention slips away really easily now.
D018-D001_h023.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D001_h023.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D001_h024.question:
I’ve been having a hard time for… I’m not even sure, maybe over a year? Time sort of blurs. I do landscaping, so I’m outside all day with machines going, and sometimes, out of nowhere, I’m not really “there.” It’s like I’m back in that moment from a few years ago when… everything went bad. I’ll be holding a trimmer and suddenly I feel like it’s happening again, the same sounds, the same panic, and it takes me a bit to realize I’m just at a client’s garden.

Since then, I carry this constant feeling that it was my fault, like I should’ve done something different. Even when people tell me I couldn’t have changed it, it doesn’t sink in. I don’t really feel happy anymore, even when good stuff happens—like finishing a big job or hanging out with mates. It just feels flat, like I’m watching someone else’s life.

I also lose my temper over stupid things—a coworker misplacing tools, traffic, a customer changing their mind. I’ll snap, then feel embarrassed after. Focusing is hard too; my mind jumps around, at work and at home, and I have to keep re-reading things or going back to check what I was doing.
D018-D001_h024.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D001_h024.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D001_h025.question:
It’s been… I’m not even sure, a few years at least, that things have felt off. Since my wife passed it’s gotten more noticeable, or maybe I just don’t have anyone to smooth things over anymore.

Little things set me off. If someone surprises me from behind in the supermarket, or if there’s a certain kind of shouting on the TV, my heart starts pounding, my hands sweat, and I feel like I have to get out of there right away. I don’t always understand why that particular sound or situation does it, but my body reacts before my head catches up.

I’m ashamed a lot of the time, like there’s something rotten about me that I can’t wash off, especially when I think back on things I went through earlier in life. I don’t talk about it; I just feel… dirty, I guess. And then other times I feel nothing at all, like someone turned the volume down on my emotions. The grandkids come over and I know I should feel happy, but it’s like I’m watching it from behind glass.

I also lose track of what I’m doing very easily now. I’ll start a task and drift off, or halfway through a conversation I realize I’ve missed what the other person was saying. That makes me snap sometimes—I raise my voice, bark at the kids on the phone, or bite the nurse’s head off for small things. I hear myself shouting and blaming, but it’s like I can’t put the brakes on until it’s already done.
D018-D001_h025.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D001_h025.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
